# Sāmaṇḍaka Saṁyutta (SN 39)
**ID:** SN 39
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Sāmaṇḍaka Saṁyutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn39
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sāmaṇḍaka Saṁyutta* (SN 39) is the thirty-ninth section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated within the *Saḷāyatanavagga* [Bodhi 2003; Jennings 1948; Mrs. Rhys Davids 1927]. The chapter consists of sixteen discourses recording dialogues set at Ukkācelā (or Ukkāvelā) on the banks of the Ganges in the Vajjian country, where the wanderer (*paribbājaka*) Sāmaṇḍaka questions the Venerable Sāriputta [Bodhi 2003; Dhammika; Jennings 1948; Mrs. Rhys Davids 1927]. Sāmaṇḍaka's inquiries cover central doctrinal topics, such as the nature of *nibbāna* (defined by Sāriputta as the destruction of lust, hatred, and delusion), arahantship, the taints (*āsava*), the definition of suffering and happiness in terms of birth and non-birth, and the difficulty of practicing the Dhamma, with each answer extolling the Noble Eightfold Path as the way to realization [Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994; Law 1931; SuttaCentral].
In structure and phrasing, this saṁyutta is practically identical to the preceding *Jambukhādaka Saṁyutta* (SN 38), differing only in the name of the wandering ascetic interlocutor [Bodhi 2003; SuttaCentral]. Because of this near-total correspondence, Pali manuscript traditions and printed editions heavily abridge the text, presenting the opening sutta and providing peyyāla instructions to expand the remaining discourses in parallel with SN 38 [Bodhi 2003; SuttaCentral].
According to SuttaCentral, the entire set of sixteen discourses (SN 39.1–16) has a single curated non-Pali parallel in the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama*, SĀ 491 (沙門出家所問) [SuttaCentral]. This cross-language alignment is also identified by DharmaNexus in the corresponding section of the *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, fascicle 18) [DharmaNexus]. Internally, DharmaNexus records extensive text reuse with SN 38 (50 matches sharing over 17,000 characters), alongside recurring formulaic parallels with the *Abyākata Saṁyutta* (SN 44), *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), and *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45) [DharmaNexus].
